title: Slope Surfer
summary: Ride the one solution curve through a beacon by finding the constant C: direct integration, separable, homogeneous and linear equations.
subject: mathematics
ncertRef: Section 9.4, Methods of solving first order, first degree differential equations
concepts: Linear equations and the integrating factor
Finding the constant from a point
learningOutcome: The student can solve a first order equation by direct integration, separation of variables, the substitution y = vx or an integrating factor, and find the constant from a point on the curve.

levels.title: Wind from x
levels.adds: Baseline: dy/dx = g(x) integrates to y = G(x) + C, and a point of the curve fixes C (Ex 9.4 Q11 to Q15; Examples 6, 7).
hints: Integrate the wind g(x) with respect to x.
Do not forget the constant C.
Put the beacon into y = G(x) + C and solve for C.

levels.title: Wind from x and y
levels.adds: New: separate the variables, integrate both sides, and fix C from the point (Ex 9.3 Q1 to Q18; Examples 4, 5).
hints: Move all the y terms to one side and all the x terms to the other.
Integrate each side and keep one constant.
Put the beacon into the general solution to get C.

levels.title: Same degree
levels.adds: New: a homogeneous equation dy/dx = F(y/x) is solved by y = vx, then the point fixes C (Ex 9.4 Q1 to Q17; Examples 10 to 13).
hints: Check that every term has the same total degree in x and y.
Put y = vx and dy/dx = v + x dv/dx, then separate v and x.
Put back v = y/x and use the beacon for C.

levels.title: Integrating factor
levels.adds: New: dy/dx + P y = Q is solved by multiplying by the integrating factor e^(∫P dx), here a power of x (Ex 9.5 Q1 to Q15; Examples 14, 15).
hints: Read P: here it is m/x, so the integrating factor is x to the power m.
The left side becomes the derivative of (factor × y).
Integrate once, then use the beacon to find C.

misconceptions: The constant of integration can be left out
Only one curve solves a differential equation
The integrating factor is always e^x
